gap: No result ChatGPT got states that no 16-inch MacBook Pro ships with a base chip: Apple's spec sheets say the 16-inch M1 Pro (2021) drives up to two external displays and today's 16-inch M5 Pro and M5 Max drive up to three and four, so the base-chip limit of one external display, which ChatGPT and UPERFECT gave as the reason to buy a driver-based extender, never applies to a 16-inch Mac.
standout_why: I compared against UPERFECT's '8 Best Triple Screen Laptop Extenders in 2026', which ChatGPT cited in chat ab-17. It says only 'base MacBook M1 and M2 chip models only support one external display' and never mentions Pro or Max chips or the 16-inch MacBook Pro. ChatGPT's own answer, which cited our current page, says 'standard M1/M2/M3 MacBooks cannot independently drive both driver-free side screens' and points to the driver-based FOPO S788 as the workaround, without noting that no 16-inch MacBook is a standard-chip model. The vendor pages ChatGPT got (FOPO S11, S788 and S788C, VueXtend Tri 16) and the Best Buy INVZI listings were either rate-limited or timed out for me (HTTP 429 or timeouts), so I could not confirm what compatibility notes they carry. The search snippets suggest the INVZI Best Buy listing names a separate adapter for base chips, but that is about base chips, not 16-inch Macs.
decides: For a 16-inch MacBook Pro owner, this confirms a driver-free dual-panel extender (two 16-inch 1920×1200 screens over USB-C or HDMI, like the INVZI MagHub Dual 16 or FOPO S11 that ChatGPT showed). It also removes the Mac-chip argument for a driver-based unit like the FOPO S788 or INVZI MagHub Trio 16, which would add a USB display driver and an extra power supply for no compatibility gain. Pick driver-based only when a Windows 16-inch laptop has fewer than two video-capable outputs. The page should open its compatibility table with: '16-inch MacBook Pro, any Apple-silicon generation: two native external displays, so driver-free works.'

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro (2021), M1 Pro: external displays
findings.value: Up to 2 external displays, up to 6K at 60 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2021) - Technical Specifications - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple quote: 'Up to two external displays with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz at over a billion colors (M1 Pro)'. This is the lowest chip Apple has ever put in an Apple-silicon 16-inch MacBook Pro.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro (2021), M1 Max: external displays
findings.value: Up to 3 external displays at up to 6K plus 1 at up to 4K 60 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2021) - Technical Specifications - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple quote: 'Up to three external displays with up to 6K resolution and one external display with up to 4K resolution at 60Hz'.

findings.label: Current 16-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Pro: external displays
findings.value: Up to 3 external displays over any mix of Thunderbolt and HDMI; one Thunderbolt port can carry all 3
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro with Liquid Retina XDR Display - Technical Specifications - Apple
findings.note: Ports: three Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) plus HDMI. The built-in display stays at full native resolution at the same time.

findings.label: Current 16-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Max: external displays
findings.value: Up to 4 external displays over any mix of Thunderbolt and HDMI
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro with Liquid Retina XDR Display - Technical Specifications - Apple
findings.note: Thunderbolt 5 ports run at DisplayPort 2.1 speeds, per the same page.

findings.label: Current 14-inch MacBook Pro, base M6: external displays (contrast)
findings.value: Up to 2 external displays over any mix of Thunderbolt and HDMI
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro with Liquid Retina XDR Display - Technical Specifications - Apple
findings.note: Even Apple's current base chip drives two external displays. The one-display limit belongs to older base M1/M2 (and M3 with the lid open) machines, none of which came in a 16-inch size.

findings.label: Apple's index of display support by model
findings.value: Apple says the number of external displays depends on the Mac model and links a spec page for each model
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Pro - Apple Support

Apple spec sheets for the 16-inch MacBook Pro with M2 Pro, M3 Pro and M4 Pro: not opened (out of tool budget). I opened only the 2021 M1 Pro/Max sheet and today's M5 Pro/Max specs page, so whether those middle generations were capped at two external displays is still to be checked.
